newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha eases on crudes, jet trading dull.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha eases on crudes, jet trading dull.

text.p: Tokyo naphtha eased on Friday, reflecting weaker overnight overseas crude markets, traders said. Naphtha prices had gained ground for three successive days.
"Today's naphtha is pretty much in line with crude," one trader said.
Open-spec naphtha for first-half March was offered at $251.50 per tonne, while bidding levels were assessed at around $250.00. It was sold at $252.50 on Thursday.
Second-half March was quoted at $247.00/248.50. On Thursday, it changed hands at $249.25.

Unionised workers at three petrochemical firms in South Korea have decided on a two-day partial strike from Tuesday. However, union representatives said the strike was not expected to cause production losses.
Japanese traders said news of the strike had little impact on the Tokyo naphtha market.

Jet kerosene trading remained dull in the absence of firm buyers. They also said two South Korean refiners each had one prompt jet cargo to sell. They said Japanese buyers were likely to hold back from the market for the time being in order to assess domestic demand trends for the rest of the month.
